s: Which one of the following correctly describes the function of HTML tags in a webpage?
o: They define and mark up the structure of text and other content
They assign numerical IP addresses to webpages
x: HTML tags mark up and structure the text and other content of webpages. Encryption and indexing are performed by other technologies or services.
tq: Distinguish the structural role of HTML from the functions of encryption, addressing and search.
sec: Web technologies - HTML tags, web server vs browser vs search engine, URL, WWW, W3C, Web 3.0  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following statements regarding web technologies:
1. A web server stores webpages and sends them when requested.
2. A web browser requests webpages and displays them on the screen.
3. A search engine indexes webpages so that they can be found.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. The server stores and serves pages, the browser displays them, and the search engine indexes them for discovery.
tq: Separate the closely related functions of the server, browser and search engine.
sec: Web technologies - HTML tags, web server vs browser vs search engine, URL, WWW, W3C, Web 3.0  [APPSC]

s: HTTP primarily specifies which of the following?
o: How messages pass between web browsers and web servers
How domain names are converted into IP addresses
How wireless devices communicate within a PAN
How e-mails are downloaded to a device
x: HTTP specifies the communication of messages between web browsers and web servers. DNS, POP3 and Bluetooth serve different functions.
tq: Match the protocol with its immediate communication function rather than with a neighbouring networking function.
sec: Web technologies - HTML tags, web server vs browser vs search engine, URL, WWW, W3C, Web 3.0  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following represents the correct order of the principal parts of a URL?
o: Protocol, domain name, path to the file
Protocol, path to the file, domain name
x: A URL contains the protocol, such as https://, followed by the domain name and the path to the file.
tq: Test the internal order of URL components instead of merely recalling its expansion.
sec: Web technologies - HTML tags, web server vs browser vs search engine, URL, WWW, W3C, Web 3.0  [APPSC]

s: The principal role of the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) is to:
o: Assign MAC addresses to network cards
Operate the global DNS root servers
x: W3C develops and maintains web standards so that webpages function consistently across different browsers.
tq: Identify the responsible body by its standard-setting function.
sec: Web technologies - HTML tags, web server vs browser vs search engine, URL, WWW, Web 3.0  [APPSC]

s:
Which of the following constitutes the core front-end technologies mentioned in relation to modern web development?
1. HTML5
2. CSS3
3. JavaScript
4. DHCP
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: HTML5, CSS3 and JavaScript are core front-end technologies. DHCP is a network protocol that assigns IP addresses automatically.
tq: Find the unrelated networking protocol among front-end web technologies.
sec: Web technologies - HTML tags, web server vs browser vs search engine, URL, WWW, W3C, Web 3.0  [APPSC]

s:
With reference to Web 3.0, consider the following statements:
1. It represents the third generation of the web.
2. It changes how the web is used, how sites are managed and how services are delivered.
3. OCEN is linked with Web 3.0 and aims to democratise lending.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Web 3.0 is the third generation of the web and involves changes in usage, site management and service delivery. OCEN seeks to democratise lending and improve credit terms for small borrowers.
tq: Combine the definition, scope and associated initiative without confusing Web 3.0 with a single application.
sec: Web technologies - HTML tags, web server vs browser vs search engine, URL, WWW, W3C, Web 3.0  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its description?
o: Surface web — not indexed by search engines
Deep web — entirely associated with illegal markets
Dark web — hidden subset of the deep web requiring tools such as Tor or I2P
Surface web — accessible only through anonymous networks
x: The dark web is a small hidden subset of the deep web and is associated with anonymous access through tools such as Tor or I2P. The surface web is indexed, while the deep web is not necessarily malicious.
tq: Use the defining access and indexing features to separate surface, deep and dark web.
sec: Web technologies - HTML tags, web server vs browser vs search engine, URL, WWW, W3C, Web 3.0  [APPSC]

s:
Arrange the following layers of the web in descending order of their approximate share:
A. Dark web
B. Surface web
C. Deep web
Select the correct sequence.
x: The deep web accounts for approximately 90–95%, the surface web about 4–5%, and the dark web is a small hidden subset.
tq: Order categories by relative size, beginning with the largest share.
sec: Web technologies - HTML tags, web server vs browser vs search engine, URL, WWW, W3C, Web 3.0  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
x: Indexed public webpages belong to the surface web, not the dark web. E-mail inboxes, net banking and intranets are examples of deep-web content.
tq: Identify the one reversed classification by applying the indexing criterion.
sec: Web technologies - HTML tags, web server vs browser vs search engine, URL, WWW, W3C, Web 3.0  [APPSC]

s: ARPANET, established in 1969, was developed under which organisation and is regarded as the forerunner of the Internet?
x: ARPANET was developed under the United States Department of Defense in 1969 and became the forerunner of the Internet.
tq: Link the historical network with its sponsoring organisation and legacy.
sec: Internet history - ARPANET, WWW inventor, first Indian ISPs  [APPSC]

s: The World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) was founded in which year?
x: Tim Berners-Lee founded the W3C in 1994. The other years correspond to ERNET, the invention of the WWW and the emergence of Satyam Infoway as a private ISP.
tq: Discriminate between closely related milestones by their years.
sec: Internet history - ARPANET, WWW inventor, first Indian ISPs  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following sequences correctly represents the Indian Internet milestones in chronological order?
o: Public internet by VSNL, ERNET, Satyam Infoway
Satyam Infoway, ERNET, public internet by VSNL
ERNET, public internet by VSNL, Satyam Infoway
ERNET, Satyam Infoway, public internet by VSNL
x: ERNET began in 1986, public internet was launched by VSNL on 15 August 1995, and Satyam Infoway became the first private ISP in 1998.
tq: Use the first, middle and last dates to establish the sequence.
sec: Internet history - ARPANET, WWW inventor, first Indian ISPs  [APPSC]

s: On which date was public Internet service launched in India by VSNL?
x: VSNL launched public Internet service in India on 15 August 1995. ERNET had been established earlier as an academic network in 1986.
tq: Distinguish the public-service launch date from the academic-network and private-ISP dates.
sec: Internet history - ARPANET, WWW inventor, first Indian ISPs  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following was India’s academic network established in 1986?
x: ERNET was India’s academic network established in 1986. VSNL launched public internet service in 1995, while Satyam Infoway became the first private ISP in 1998.
tq: Match the network name with its historical category and year.
sec: Internet history - ARPANET, WWW inventor, first Indian ISPs  [APPSC]

s: Which notation is characteristic of an IPv4 address?
o: Six hexadecimal pairs separated by hyphens
Four decimal octets separated by dots
A domain name followed by a file path
Eight hexadecimal groups separated by colons
x: IPv4 uses dotted-decimal notation, such as 192.168.1.1. IPv6 uses eight hexadecimal groups separated by colons, whereas six hexadecimal pairs describe a MAC address.
tq: Separate the notations of IPv4, IPv6 and MAC addressing.
sec: IP and MAC addressing - IPv4 vs IPv6, MAC length, notation, classes  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following correctly describes an IPv6 address?
o: A 64-bit address used only for multicast
A 48-bit address burnt into a network card
A 32-bit address written only in dotted decimal
A 128-bit address written as eight hexadecimal groups separated by colons
x: IPv6 is 128 bits long and is written as eight hexadecimal groups separated by colons. A 48-bit physical address refers to MAC addressing.
tq: Use length and notation together to distinguish IPv6 from IPv4 and MAC addresses.
sec: IP and MAC addressing - IPv4 vs IPv6, MAC length, notation, classes  [APPSC]

s: A MAC address is best described as a:
o: 48-bit physical address burnt into the network card and used at the data link layer
16-bit address used only by web browsers
32-bit logical address used at the network layer
x: A MAC address is a 48-bit physical address, equal to 6 bytes or 12 hexadecimal digits, generally burnt into the network card and used at the data link layer.
tq: Combine the address length, physical nature and OSI-layer association.
sec: IP and MAC addressing - IPv4 vs IPv6, MAC length, notation, classes  [APPSC]

s:
Which of the following pairs correctly represents IPv4 address classes by their first-octet ranges?
1. Class A — 1 to 126
2. Class B — 128 to 191
3. Class C — 192 to 223
4. Class D — 240 to 255
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Classes A, B and C have ranges 1–126, 128–191 and 192–223 respectively. Class D is 224–239 for multicast; 240–255 is Class E for experimental use.
tq: Check each numerical range against the class boundary, especially the swapped D and E ranges.
sec: IP and MAC addressing - IPv4 vs IPv6, MAC length, notation, classes  [APPSC]

s: The address range 224–239 in IPv4 is associated with:
x: The first-octet range 224–239 constitutes Class D, used for multicast. Class E occupies 240–255, while 127.x.x.x is reserved for loopback.
tq: Test the boundary ranges of the IPv4 classes directly.
sec: IP and MAC addressing - IPv4 vs IPv6, MAC length, notation, classes  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
x: The 127.x.x.x range is used for loopback. Class D multicast is 224–239, Class E experimental is 240–255, and 192–223 is Class C.
tq: Find the correctly matched exception among deliberately interchanged class ranges.
sec: IP and MAC addressing - IPv4 vs IPv6, MAC length, notation, classes  [APPSC]

s: DNS performs which of the following functions?
o: Assigns MAC addresses to network cards
Converts human-readable domain names into numerical IP addresses
x: DNS acts as the Internet’s directory by translating human-readable domain names into numerical IP addresses.
tq: Identify the service needed when a user knows a name but the network requires an IP address.
sec: IP and MAC addressing - IPv4 vs IPv6, MAC length, notation, classes  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the wireless standard?
x: Bluetooth uses IEEE 802.15.1 and is a personal area network technology. Wi-Fi uses IEEE 802.11 and is associated with wireless LANs.
tq: Start from the standard number to distinguish Bluetooth from Wi-Fi.
sec: Wireless standards - Bluetooth vs Wi-Fi bands and versions, 2.4 GHz devices  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following statements regarding Bluetooth and Wi-Fi:
1. Bluetooth generally has a short range of about 10 metres for a class 2 device.
2. Wi-Fi generally provides coverage over a longer range, such as a whole building.
3. Bluetooth operates only in the 5 GHz band.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Bluetooth class 2 devices have a short range of approximately 10 metres, while Wi-Fi generally covers a larger area. Bluetooth operates in the 2.4 GHz ISM band, not only in 5 GHz.
tq: Use range and frequency comparisons to reject the absolute frequency claim.
sec: Wireless standards - Bluetooth vs Wi-Fi bands and versions, 2.4 GHz devices  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following statements about Wi-Fi frequency bands is correct?
o: Wi-Fi operates only in the 6 GHz band.
Wi-Fi uses the 2.4 GHz band only for Bluetooth compatibility.
Wi-Fi operates in 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands, with 6 GHz available in Wi-Fi 6E.
Wi-Fi operates only in the 2.4 GHz band.
x: Wi-Fi uses the 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands; Wi-Fi 6E also includes the 6 GHz band. Bluetooth uses the 2.4 GHz ISM band.
tq: Test the frequency-band comparison and the Wi-Fi 6E exception.
sec: Wireless standards - Bluetooth vs Wi-Fi bands and versions, 2.4 GHz devices  [APPSC]

s:
Which of the following devices commonly operates in the 2.4 GHz range?
1. Microwave oven
2. Cordless phone
3. Bluetooth device
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Microwave ovens, cordless phones and Bluetooth devices are among the devices associated with the 2.4 GHz range.
tq: Use the shared-band idea to identify all applicable devices.
sec: Wireless standards - Bluetooth vs Wi-Fi bands and versions, 2.4 GHz devices  [APPSC]

s: The 2019 APPSC key identified which version as the latest version of Bluetooth?
x: The 2019 APPSC key treated Bluetooth 5.1 as the latest version. This is a time-specific reference and should not be confused with later versions.
tq: Recognise the dated examination reference rather than applying an unspecified current-version claim.
sec: Wireless standards - Bluetooth vs Wi-Fi bands and versions, 2.4 GHz devices  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following technologies links devices directly without requiring a LAN?
x: Wi-Fi Direct enables devices to connect directly without a LAN. DNS resolves names, DHCP assigns IP addresses and Li-Fi transmits data through LED light.
tq: Select the technology that satisfies the stated direct-connect requirement.
sec: Wireless standards - Bluetooth vs Wi-Fi bands and versions, 2.4 GHz devices  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes Li-Fi from Wi-Fi?
o: Li-Fi carries data on LED light and can provide better bandwidth and security than Wi-Fi.
Li-Fi operates only through telephone lines and has no wireless application.
Li-Fi is a form of DNS-based addressing.
Li-Fi is restricted to Bluetooth personal area networks.
x: Li-Fi transmits data using LED light and is described as offering better bandwidth and security than Wi-Fi.
tq: Use the transmission medium to distinguish Li-Fi from radio-based Wi-Fi.
sec: Wireless standards - Bluetooth vs Wi-Fi bands and versions, 2.4 GHz devices  [APPSC]

s: NFC is characterised by which of the following features?
o: Operation over several kilometres at gigabit speed
Operation only at a few centimetres with a rate of 106–424 kbps
Operation throughout a building using 5 GHz only
x: NFC works only over a few centimetres and has a stated data rate of 106–424 kbps.
tq: Combine the very short range with the specified data-rate interval.
sec: Wireless standards - Bluetooth vs Wi-Fi bands and versions, 2.4 GHz devices  [APPSC]

s: Which protocol is primarily used for reliable delivery of data in the TCP/IP suite?
x: Within TCP/IP, TCP ensures reliable delivery, while IP addresses and routes packets.
tq: Separate the transport reliability function of TCP from the addressing and routing function of IP.
sec: Protocols → function; protocol elements  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following protocols transfers webpages, with its secure version encrypting browser-server traffic through TLS?
x: HTTP transfers webpages, while HTTPS encrypts browser-server traffic using TLS.
tq: Match the protocol pair with web transfer and security rather than with mail or file transfer.
sec: Protocols → function; protocol elements  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: POP3 — downloading mail to one device, usually deleting it from the server
IMAP — permanently deleting mail from the server after downloading it to one device
x: IMAP keeps mail on the server and synchronises it across devices. POP3 generally downloads mail to one device and usually deletes it from the server.
tq: Distinguish the confusable mail protocols by their treatment of messages on the server.
sec: Protocols → function; protocol elements  [APPSC]

s: A user wants the same e-mail account to remain synchronised across several devices. Which protocol is most suitable?
x: IMAP keeps mail on the server and synchronises it across devices. POP3 is generally intended for downloading mail to one device.
tq: Infer the protocol from the practical requirement of multi-device synchronisation.
sec: Protocols → function; protocol elements  [APPSC]

s: Which protocol automatically assigns IP addresses to devices on a network?
x: DHCP assigns IP addresses automatically. DNS translates names into IP addresses, while HTTP and TCP perform different communication functions.
tq: Identify the protocol by its automatic address-assignment function.
sec: Protocols → function; protocol elements  [APPSC]

s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (Protocol element)
A. Syntax
B. Semantics
C. Timing

List-II (Meaning)
1. Meaning of each field
2. Format of data
3. When and how fast to send

option_a
x: Syntax specifies the format of data, semantics specifies the meaning of each field, and timing specifies when and how fast data is sent.
tq: Start from the sure pair ‘syntax–format’ and complete the protocol-element mapping.
sec: Protocols → function; protocol elements  [APPSC]

s:
Assertion (A): HTTPS provides greater security for browser-server communication than HTTP.
Reason (R): HTTPS encrypts the traffic between the browser and the server through TLS.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: Both statements are true, and TLS-based encryption directly explains why HTTPS provides greater security than HTTP.
tq: Check whether the reason directly explains the security difference between HTTP and HTTPS.
sec: Protocols → function; protocol elements  [APPSC]

s: A network confined to the personal devices of an individual, generally using Bluetooth, is known as:
x: PAN stands for Personal Area Network and connects an individual's nearby devices, commonly through Bluetooth.
tq: Use the coverage-area clue to distinguish network types.
sec: Network types and topologies - PAN, LAN, MAN, WAN, VPN  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following correctly represents the usual geographical coverage of a MAN?
x: A Metropolitan Area Network (MAN) generally covers a city, placing it between a LAN and a WAN in geographical extent.
tq: Split the options by geographical scale.
sec: Network types and topologies - PAN, LAN, MAN, WAN, VPN  [APPSC]

s: A network that spans a large geographical area and links LANs at different locations is called:
x: A Wide Area Network (WAN) connects networks over large areas; the Internet is an example of a global WAN.
tq: Match the definition with the widest network category.
sec: Network types and topologies - PAN, LAN, MAN, WAN, VPN  [APPSC]

s: A Virtual Private Network primarily provides:
o: A replacement for all network protocols
A wireless connection restricted to one room
A physical cable exclusively owned by a user
An encrypted tunnel over a public network
x: A VPN creates an encrypted tunnel through a public network, improving the privacy of communication.
tq: Identify the function rather than the physical form of the network.
sec: Network types and topologies - PAN, LAN, MAN, WAN, VPN  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following statements regarding network topologies:
1. In a bus topology, all nodes share one backbone cable.
2. In a star topology, failure of one node normally isolates the entire network.
3. In a ring topology, each node is linked to two neighbouring nodes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. In a star topology, failure of one node is generally isolated; failure of the central hub can stop the network.
tq: Find the incorrect resilience statement before selecting the code.
sec: Network types and topologies - PAN, LAN, MAN, WAN, VPN  [APPSC]

s: Which topology is characterised by every node being connected to every other node?
x: In a mesh topology, every node is linked to every other node, making it highly resilient but costly.
tq: Use the complete-connectivity clue.
sec: Network types and topologies - PAN, LAN, MAN, WAN, VPN  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Tree topology — It has no hierarchical structure
Bus topology — Failure of one node isolates only that node
Star topology — Failure of the central hub can stop all nodes
Ring topology — Every node is connected to every other node
x: In a star topology, all nodes depend on the central hub or switch; its failure can stop the entire network.
tq: Test the resilience consequence associated with each layout.
sec: Network types and topologies - PAN, LAN, MAN, WAN, VPN  [APPSC]

s: A tree topology is best described as:
o: A single circular connection of nodes
A topology in which every node has a direct link to every other node
A network using only one backbone cable
x: A tree topology combines star networks in a hierarchy. Failure of a parent can affect the branch below it.
tq: Match the structural description with the topology name.
sec: Network types and topologies - PAN, LAN, MAN, WAN, VPN  [APPSC]

s: ICANN, established in 1998 as a United States non-profit organisation, is primarily associated with:
o: Coordinating the global domain name system and IP address allocation
x: ICANN coordinates the global Domain Name System and IP address allocation. It was established in 1998 as a US non-profit organisation.
tq: Use the organisation-function and year combination.
sec: Internet governance - ICANN, NIXI and .in, Universal Acceptance, IDNs (BhashaNet)  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following statements about NIXI:
1. It was established in 2003.
2. It is a not-for-profit organisation under MeitY.
3. It runs the .in registry and IRINN.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: NIXI was established in 2003, functions as a not-for-profit organisation under MeitY, and runs Internet exchange points, the .in registry and IRINN.
tq: Check each institutional detail before choosing the combined code.
sec: Internet governance - ICANN, NIXI and .in, Universal Acceptance, IDNs (BhashaNet)  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following is NOT a function associated with NIXI?
o: Coordinating the entire global DNS and global IP allocation system
x: NIXI performs Indian Internet exchange, .in registry and IRINN functions. Global DNS coordination and global IP allocation are associated with ICANN.
tq: Separate the national Internet institution from the global coordinating body.
sec: Internet governance - ICANN, NIXI and .in, Universal Acceptance, IDNs (BhashaNet)  [APPSC]

s: An Internationalised Domain Name (IDN) is a domain name that:
o: Works only without an Internet connection
Can be written only in hexadecimal characters
x: IDNs permit domain names in local scripts, such as .Bharat written in Devanagari.
tq: Use the meaning of 'internationalised' in the domain-name context.
sec: Internet governance - ICANN, NIXI and .in, Universal Acceptance, IDNs (BhashaNet)  [APPSC]

s: Universal Acceptance in the context of Internet governance means that:
o: All Internet content must be available without authentication
Every application and e-mail system should accept all valid domain names and e-mail IDs, including those in local scripts
Every country must use one common domain name
Only English-language domain names can be accessed universally
x: Universal Acceptance ensures that applications and e-mail systems correctly accept all valid domain names and e-mail IDs, including IDNs.
tq: Identify the inclusive technical standard rather than a content policy.
sec: Internet governance - ICANN, NIXI and .in, Universal Acceptance, IDNs (BhashaNet)  [APPSC]

s: BhashaNet, associated with MeitY and NIXI and launched in 2022, promotes:
o: Exclusive use of English on the Internet
x: BhashaNet promotes Universal Acceptance and the use of Indian-language Internet domain names and e-mail IDs; it is associated with MeitY-NIXI and the year 2022.
tq: Combine the initiative, institutional partners and objective.
sec: Internet governance - ICANN, NIXI and .in, Universal Acceptance, IDNs (BhashaNet)  [APPSC]

s:
Which provisions are associated with governmental blocking of online content in India?
1. Section 69A of the Information Technology Act, 2000
2. Section 79 of the Information Technology Act, 2000
3. Section 3 of the Telegraph Act, 1885
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Sections 69A and 79 of the Information Technology Act, 2000 are associated with orders to ISPs and intermediaries for blocking content. Section 3 of the Telegraph Act is not the stated blocking provision.
tq: Eliminate the unrelated statutory provision.
sec: Internet governance - ICANN, NIXI and .in, Universal Acceptance, IDNs (BhashaNet)  [APPSC]

s: Which legislation replaced the Telegraph Act, 1885 and contains the power to suspend Internet services?
x: The Telecommunications Act, 2023 replaced the Telegraph Act and contains the power to suspend Internet services.
tq: Distinguish content-blocking provisions from the later telecommunications legislation.
sec: Internet governance - ICANN, NIXI and .in, Universal Acceptance, IDNs (BhashaNet)  [APPSC]

s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Device)
a. Hub
b. Switch
c. Router
d. Modem

List-II (Primary role)
i. Routes packets using IP
 ii. Converts digital and analogue signals
 iii. Broadcasts data to all ports
 iv. Forwards frames using MAC addresses

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: A hub broadcasts to all ports, a switch forwards frames by MAC address, a router routes using IP, and a modem converts between digital and analogue signals.
tq: Start from the sure device-function pairs and complete the code.
sec: Network devices and transmission - router, switch, hub, modem, duplex, DSL/cable/fibre  [other exams]

s: A repeater is used primarily to:
x: A repeater regenerates a weak signal and operates at the Physical layer.
tq: Match the device with its signal-level function.
sec: Network devices and transmission - router, switch, hub, modem, duplex, DSL/cable/fibre  [other exams]

s: A gateway differs from a router chiefly because a gateway:
o: Operates only as a physical cable
Broadcasts every frame to all ports
x: A gateway joins networks that use different protocols and may operate across all or upper OSI layers.
tq: Discriminate between two nearby networking devices by their interoperability function.
sec: Network devices and transmission - router, switch, hub, modem, duplex, DSL/cable/fibre  [other exams]

s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with its transmission mode?
1. Radio or television broadcast — Simplex
2. Walkie-talkie — Half duplex
3. Telephone conversation — Full duplex
Select the correct answer.
x: Simplex permits one-way transmission, half duplex permits two-way transmission one at a time, and full duplex permits simultaneous two-way transmission.
tq: Compare the direction and simultaneity of communication.
sec: Network devices and transmission - router, switch, hub, modem, duplex, DSL/cable/fibre  [other exams]

s: Which transmission mode is used when communication can occur in both directions, but not simultaneously?
x: Half duplex permits communication in both directions, but one direction operates at a time, as in a walkie-talkie.
tq: Focus on the phrase 'both ways, one at a time'.
sec: Network devices and transmission - router, switch, hub, modem, duplex, DSL/cable/fibre  [other exams]

s:
Consider the following statements about Internet connection media:
1. DSL uses telephone copper lines.
2. Cable Internet uses coaxial television cable.
3. Fibre Internet transmits data as light pulses through optical fibre.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: DSL uses telephone copper lines, cable Internet uses coaxial TV cable, and fibre Internet uses optical fibre carrying light pulses.
tq: Match each technology with its physical transmission medium.
sec: Network devices and transmission - router, switch, hub, modem, duplex, DSL/cable/fibre  [other exams]

s: Satellite Internet generally consists of which three segments?
x: Satellite Internet has space, ground and user (VSAT) segments and does not require a terrestrial wire connection.
tq: Recall the three-part system architecture.
sec: Network devices and transmission - router, switch, hub, modem, duplex, DSL/cable/fibre  [other exams]

s: Which of the following represents the correct top-to-bottom order of the OSI model?
o: Application, Presentation, Session, Transport, Network, Data Link, Physical
Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application
Application, Session, Presentation, Network, Transport, Data Link, Physical
Presentation, Application, Session, Transport, Data Link, Network, Physical
x: From the top layer downward, the OSI model is Application, Presentation, Session, Transport, Network, Data Link and Physical.
tq: Use the first and last layers, then verify the middle sequence.
sec: OSI model - seven layers → protocols/devices  [other exams]

s:
Match the following OSI layers with their associated functions or protocols:
List-I (Layer)
a. Presentation
b. Session
c. Transport
d. Data Link

List-II (Function or protocol)
i. TCP and UDP
ii. Encryption, compression and formats
 iii. Opens and closes sessions
 iv. MAC addressing and frame forwarding

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: The Presentation layer handles encryption, compression and formats; the Session layer opens and closes sessions; the Transport layer uses TCP and UDP; and the Data Link layer handles MAC-based frame operations.
tq: Start with the distinctive TCP/UDP and MAC pairs.
sec: OSI model - seven layers → protocols/devices  [other exams]

s:
Which of the following is correctly matched with the OSI layer?
1. HTTP — Application layer
2. IP — Network layer
3. MAC — Data Link layer
4. Cables — Physical layer
Select the correct answer.
x: HTTP is an Application-layer protocol, IP belongs to the Network layer, MAC is associated with the Data Link layer, and cables operate at the Physical layer.
tq: Use protocol and device layer matching to validate each statement.
sec: OSI model - seven layers → protocols/devices  [other exams]

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
x: A modem is associated with the Physical layer because it modulates and demodulates signals; it is not a Transport-layer device.
tq: Find the device placed at the wrong OSI layer.
sec: OSI model - seven layers → protocols/devices  [other exams]

s: An organisation notices that a particular website is inaccessible to users of one Internet service provider, while users of another provider can access it. Which explanation is consistent with this situation?
o: The provider may be using DNS poisoning, HTTP interception or SNI filtering
The OSI model has ceased to operate for that website
